summary: THE FIT IS MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES, ON THE SAME LINES, AND IT IS ZERO. cecad.meshfeatures.intervals ray-cast calipers were run through BOTH sole_left.stl and foot_left.stl on 75 identical lines (54 y-lines at z -19/-20/-21/-22/-23/-24 across x 34..66 step 4; 21 x-lines at z -19/-21/-23 across y -6..37), giving 150 gaps between the socket's inner wall and the plug's outer wall: min -0.0020, max +0.0020, mean -0.000007 mm. The two walls are one surface to the 0.002 mm the decimated STL can express. Section 36.8000 x 49.8000 mm (x 31.6000..68.4000, y -9.9000..39.9000), constant at every meshslice z-section from -18.342 to -24.0. Rim plane z -18.3419 (0 segments at -18.3419, 659 at -18.3421). Socket wall 1.594-2.479 mm, mean 2.0165, 2.1000 plateau on the long walls. Floor 2.000 +/- 0.001 mm of TPU at nine stations, independently agreeing with the sole folder's own 27x31 grid. Depth 7.9170 mm (toe) to 10.6550 mm (heel). compat.py graded the real pair live: interface_names, section, fit, engagement_depth and socket_section PASS.
by: claude (microduck lane T), cecad.meshfeatures + meshslice on Pollen's meshes

summary: THE SOLE IS HELD ON BY NOTHING BUT FRICTION AND THAT FRICTION IS UNMEASURED. cecad.meshfeatures.cylinders on sole_left.stl finds NO hole of any diameter through the socket wall or floor; there is no barb, no groove and no adhesive named anywhere in the reference. The ankle group's only screw is the single M2 at (x 50.0000, y 4.5020) that hangs the FOOT from the ANKLE (part:microduck-ankle-left `foot_screw` -> part:microduck-foot-left `ankle_screw`) and it does not pass through the sole. So retention is a zero-clearance interference between a printed TPU socket and a printed PLA plug: set by the two processes' as-built dimensions and the elastomer's modulus, none of which is in any file here. pull_off_N stays MISSING rather than being estimated. What settles it: pull a real sole off a real foot on a gauge and state pull_off_N on the socket interface.

A 0.2539 mm OVERLAP AT THE FLOOR, RECORDED NOT AVERAGED. The foot's ribs reach z -29.2509 (its own bbox minimum) while the sole's inner floor at that station (x 35, y 15) is -28.9970. Two readings fit and nothing here separates them: deliberate squeeze into the elastomer, or an overlap in the visual meshes. Pollen's MJCF holds the two as separate rigid geoms and resolves no penetration. Also recorded: lane T's own corner circle fits at z -19.0 and -22.0 were REJECTED rather than published — the fit windows catch the internal ribs as well as the wall and the residual mean came out 0.13-1.05 mm, a worse instrument than the one the part folders already used for R3.4/R4.9 (socket) and R3.45/R4.89 (plug). A worse measurement does not replace a better one. What settles the overlap: measure a real pair, or establish whether the sole floor is compressed when the foot is home.

THE FOLDER WORKS THROUGH THE ONE INTEGRATION SEAM, not just when run directly. cecad.triad.mate("connection:press-fit-sole-foot", a_iface, b_iface, params) — TRIAD.md's single seam, the call every other app (ce-struct, ce-pcb, ce-wire, the APIs) reaches this folder through — was invoked live on the reference interface pair on 2026-09-02 and mate() returned dof_left [], adds [], holds_by 'friction' — a prism in a prism leaves nothing free, and the joint adds no fastener because the meshes carry none. Run in FreeCAD's python 3.11 with CE_TRIAD_ROOT set to this repo plus ce-workshop. All four connection folders authored in this lane were exercised the same way in the same run and all four returned; none raised.
by: claude (microduck lane T), cecad.triad.mate through the loader
